targets.semantic_primary: Simple random walk on the Cayley graph of the lamplighter group Z with the standard generators has return probability p_{2n}(o,o) at least exp(-C n^{1/3}) for some constant C and every n.
targets.question_verbatim: Show that simple random walk $(\Psi_j,X_j)$ on the Cayley graph of $\Z^{\odot}$ (with the standard generators) satisfies $p_{2n}(o,o)\ge\exp(-Cn^{1/3})$ for some $C$ and all $n$. (The matching upper bound was proved in Corollary 6.32(iii).)
targets.scope: The single displayed inequality of Exercise 6.78, for simple random walk on the Cayley graph of the lamplighter group with the standard generators. The parenthetical reference to Corollary 6.32(iii) is the author pointing at the matching upper bound, not a second target, and the exercise number 6.78 appears nowhere else in the 716-page source except its Comment, so no body theorem carries the same target.
ambient_hypotheses: The walk is simple random walk on the Cayley graph of the lamplighter group with the standard generators; the two-sided in n index p_{2n} and the quantifier "for all n" are as printed.

functional_definitions.the lamplighter group Z^odot: the restricted wreath product (direct sum over Z of Z_2) semidirect Z, with group operation (psi,m)(psi',m') = (psi (+) S^{-m} psi', m+m'), defined in the chapter body at physical p. 106 (printed p. 89) and reprinted as uncounted context in the reader
functional_definitions.the standard generators: the three generators {(0,1),(0,-1),(1_{0},0)} named on physical p. 106
functional_definitions.p_n(o,o): the probability that the walk started at the identity o is at o at time n; the exercise writes p_{2n} and the Comment writes p_n, and neither index is changed in the reader
functional_definitions.C: a positive constant the exercise does not identify and the reader does not identify; the Comment produces it from its own c and c_1

targets.author_supply_reused: The complete author Comment on physical p. 637 (printed p. 620): a one-block confinement estimate P_v[max_{j<=r^2}|X_j| <= 2r and |X_{r^2}| <= r] >= e^{-c} for every v in [-r,r], iteration of the Markov property at multiples of r^2 to get e^{-c ceil(n/r^2)}, the last-visit lamp-extinguishing and return-to-origin requirement giving p_n(o,o) >= exp(-cn/r^2 - c_1 r), and the optimisation r = n^{1/3}. Reprinted in full in readers/6_78/reader.tex as the primary proof.
targets.method_not_separate_target: The Comment contains one route only; there is no second author solution, so nothing is counted as an alternative target.
targets.excluded_refinement: The absorbed ceiling ceil(n/r^2) -> n/r^2 + 1, the assembly of the exercise constant C from the Comment c and c_1, and the substitution of 2n for n in the final displayed estimate are recorded by the adjudication as mechanical. They are not added to the reader and are not part of the counted target; all three residues stay literal.
